title: The Ophiuchus DIsc Survey Employing ALMA (ODISEA) - I: project description and continuum images at 28 au resolution
question: What are the 1.3 mm continuum fluxes, sizes, substructures and implied dust masses of the Spitzer-selected (Sample A) discs in Ophiuchus at 0.2'' resolution?

what.value: Spitzer catalog, 2MASS and Spitzer photometry of the 147 targets

evidence.quote: Table [\[table:c2d\]](#table:c2d) shows the 2MASS and *Spitzer* photometry from these 147 objects, taken from the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive.

what.value: Spectral types and companion separations from literature

evidence.quote: We have also collected spectral types from the literature for 88 objects from our sample.

external_data.citation: Cieza et al. 2010; Erickson et al. 2011; Wilking et al. 2005; Manara et al. 2015; McClure et al. 2010 and others

what.value: Dust masses of other regions for comparison (Lupus, Upper Sco, Cha I, sigma Ori, IC 348, Taurus)

evidence.quote: For comparison, we perform the same analysis for objects in Lupus (Ansdell et al. 2016), Upper Scorpius (Barenfeld et al. 2016), Chamaeleon I (Pascucci et al. 2016)

external_data.citation: Ansdell et al. 2016; Barenfeld et al. 2016; Pascucci et al. 2016; Ansdell et al. 2017; Ruiz-Rodriguez et al. 2018; Andrews et al. 2013

recipe.method: Inspect images with CASA Viewer; imstat peak within 1'' aperture and rms in 1.0-1.2'' annulus

recipe.goal: Fit fluxes and sizes of single sources in the uv plane
recipe.method: uvmodelfit point source and Gaussian fits for single objects with peak S/N>5; resolved only if S/N>30 and Gaussian flux > point flux + 3 rms; elliptical disc model for substructured sources
key_parameters: Free parameters: flux, major/minor FWHM, PA, offsets <1''

recipe.goal: Photometry of multiples and substructured discs, and non-detections
recipe.method: CASA Viewer 2-D image-plane fitting for multiples and ~3'' apertures for substructured discs; point-source uvmodelfit at offset-corrected positions (-0.08'', -0.56'') for non-detections
Mean of each pixel from the images of the 27 non-detections centered at nominal positions
Phase-only self-calibration and uniform-weight imaging for ~50 sources >~15 mJy; visual inspection; deprojected radial profiles using fitted PA and axes

recipe.goal: Convert flux to dust mass and compare regions
recipe.method: Optically thin M_dust = F d^2/(kappa B(T)); Kaplan-Meier cumulative distributions with ASURV
key_parameters: kappa_1.3mm = 0.023 cm2/g (beta=1), d = 140 pc, T_dust = 20 K
assumptions: Optically thin emission, T=20 K, beta=1, Beckwith opacity, 140 pc

evidence.loc: 3.1 Continuum images, disc photometry, and sizes
evidence.quote: We detect a total of 133 discs in 120 systems.
Fifty-three of these discs are spatially resolved.
The stacked image has an rms of 0.04 mJy and shows a 4-$\sigma$ (0.16 mJy) detection
corresponds to an average dust mass of just 0.09 M$_{\oplus}$.
We find clear substructures (inner cavities, rings, gaps, and/or spiral arms) in 8 of the sources and hints of such structures in another 4 discs.

answer_key.quantity: Discs with dust mass sufficient for 10 Earth-mass core

evidence.loc: 4.3 Implications for planet formation: challenges and future directions
evidence.quote: only $\sim$50 targets (1/3 of the sample) have enough dust to form a critical-mass rocky core
